subject: SPDE object for non stationary/ Anisotropic Model

messages.author: 96e275f43eafb053
messages.subject: SPDE object for non stationary/ Anisotropic Model
parts:
Hi All,

I am constructing a non stationary/anisotropic  SPDE object using the following code:

basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2,degree=2)

spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha=2,B.tau=cbind(0, basis.T, basis.K*0),
                         B.kappa=cbind(0, basis.T*0, basis.K/2))

When  model is run, INLA crashes.

Is my approach wrong ?

Thanks

messages.author: 96e275f43eafb053
messages.subject: Re: SPDE object for non stationary/ Anisotropic Model
parts:
The error causing the model to crash is:
*** ERROR *** 	INLA.Data1: Binomial data[279] (nb,y) = (-2.14748e+09,79) is void

I have run the following model
formula=(Pf ~ -1 + Intercept + Long+ Lat + prec+urbanization + f(field, model = spde, group = field.group, control.group =list(model="ar",order=2)))

Ntrials=c(civ.validation$Ex, rep(NA,13039))

model_anisotropy=inla(formula, data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
                      family = "binomial", Ntrials=Ntrials,
                      control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),link = 1,
                                               compute=TRUE),control.compute=list(cpo=T,dic=TRUE),  
                      keep=FALSE,verbose=TRUE)

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE object for non stationary/ Anisotropic Model
parts:
On Fri, 2014-04-25 at 01:16 -0700, K.e wrote:
> The error causing the model to crash is:
> *** ERROR *** INLA.Data1: Binomial data[279] (nb,y) = (-2.14748e+09,79) is void
>

what this says is that the Binomial observation is 79, but the size is
-2.14748e+09, which is not a legal value. so the the inla-program does
not crash, it stops ;-)

Fix your input and it should be fine ;-)

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE object for non stationary/ Anisotropic Model
parts:
You should construct Ntrials in inla.stack() to make sure it gets the right size and contents.
That is a potiantial source of the problem.
See the example at the end of the second spde tutorial on r-inla.org for a basic example.

Finn
